question:
Ratha Jatra, the festival of Chariots of Lord Jagannatha is celebrated every year in
______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puri, Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ratha Jatra (Chariot Festival) of Lord Jagannatha is celebrated every year at Puri, Odisha, on the Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya (second day of the bright fortnight of Ashadha month). (रथ यात्रा — भगवान जगन्नाथ की रथयात्रा, पुरी)

 

• Three deities — Lord Jagannatha, Balabhadra (Balarama) and Subhadra — are taken out of the Jagannath Temple in huge, elaborately decorated wooden chariots and pulled by devotees to the Gundicha Temple, about 3 km away.

 

• The chariot of Lord Jagannatha is called Nandighosha, Balabhadra's is Taladhwaja, and Subhadra's is Darpadalana.

 

• Puri's Jagannath Temple is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites of Hinduism, along with Badrinath, Dwarka and Rameswaram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The English word "juggernaut" (something unstoppable) derives from the massive, seemingly unstoppable Ratha Jatra chariots.

 

• Similar Ratha Yatra celebrations are now also held in other Indian cities and abroad, but the original and most famous one is at Puri.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Sarnath is famous as the place where Gautam Buddha gave his first sermon, not for Ratha Jatra.

 

• Jaipur, Rajasthan (Option 3): Jaipur is known for festivals like Teej and the Elephant Festival, not Ratha Jatra.

 

• Kolkata, West Bengal (Option 4): Kolkata hosts a Ratha Yatra as well (notably at ISKCON), but it is not the original or primary site associated with this festival.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the production possibility
frontier?
I. It gives the combinations between two goods that can be produced when the
resources of the economy are fully utilised.
II. It illustrates the production possibilities of the economy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF), also called the Production Possibility Curve (PPC), shows the maximum possible combinations of two goods that an economy can produce when all its resources are fully and efficiently utilised with a given technology. (उत्पादन संभावना वक्र)

 

• Statement I is correct: PPF gives exactly such combinations of two goods under full resource utilisation.

 

• Statement II is also correct: the PPF is, by definition, the graphical illustration of an economy's production possibilities — i.e., what combinations it is capable of producing.

 

• Points on the curve represent efficient production, points inside the curve represent underutilisation of resources, and points outside the curve are unattainable with current resources/technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The PPF is typically concave to the origin because of the law of increasing opportunity cost — as more resources shift to producing one good, increasingly larger amounts of the other good must be sacrificed.

 

• A rightward shift of the entire PPF represents economic growth, arising from more resources, better technology, or improved efficiency.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect because Statement II is also a correct description of the PPF, not merely Statement I.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect because Statement I is also a correct description of the PPF, not merely Statement II.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect because both statements accurately describe the production possibility frontier.

question: Which among the following is NOT a crop as classified in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Crops in India are classified into three main cropping seasons: Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid. (फसल मौसम — खरीफ, रबी, जायद)

 

• Kharif crops are sown at the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in autumn (September–October); examples include rice, maize, cotton and jowar.

 

• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–November) and harvested in spring (March–April); examples include wheat, barley, mustard and gram.

 

• Zaid crops are short-duration summer crops grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons (March–June); examples include watermelon, cucumber and fodder crops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The classification of crops into these three seasons is based on India's monsoon-dependent agricultural cycle.

 

• Some states with distinct climates (e.g., Tamil Nadu with its northeast monsoon) follow a somewhat different agricultural calendar.

 

NOTE

 

• Zaid (Option 1): A genuine, officially recognised short summer cropping season in India.

 

• Kharif (Option 2): A genuine, officially recognised monsoon cropping season in India.

 

• Rabi (Option 3): A genuine, officially recognised winter cropping season in India.

question: Which of the following statements regarding river Ganga is correct?
option_1: Ghaghara is a tributary coming from peninsular uplands.
option_2: Yamuna is a right bank tributary meets the Ganga at Allahabad.
option_3: The length of the Ganga is over 5000 km.
option_4: Betwa is a tributary of river Ganga rising from the Himalayas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yamuna is a right bank tributary meets the Ganga at Allahabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Yamuna, the largest tributary of the Ganga, is a right-bank tributary that rises from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad), forming the sacred confluence known as the Triveni Sangam. (त्रिवेणी संगम — गंगा-यमुना का मिलन स्थान, प्रयागराज)

 

• The Ghaghara (Sarayu) river is actually a Himalayan (left-bank) tributary of the Ganga, not one arising from the peninsular uplands.

 

• The length of the Ganga is about 2,525 km, making it one of the longest rivers in India, but well under 5000 km.

 

• The Betwa river rises in the Vindhya Range (Madhya Pradesh), a peninsular/plateau region, and is a tributary of the Yamuna, not directly of the Ganga, and it does not originate in the Himalayas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major left-bank (Himalayan) tributaries of the Ganga include the Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi; major right-bank (peninsular) tributaries include the Yamuna, Son, and Chambal (via Yamuna).

 

• The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh) in Uttarakhand and empties into the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghaghara is a tributary coming from peninsular uplands (Option 1): Incorrect; the Ghaghara is a Himalayan tributary of the Ganga.

 

• The length of the Ganga is over 5000 km (Option 3): Incorrect; the Ganga's length is approximately 2,525 km.

 

• Betwa is a tributary of river Ganga rising from the Himalayas (Option 4): Incorrect; the Betwa rises in the Vindhya Range and is a tributary of the Yamuna, not a Himalayan river.

question:
Which Article of the Indian constitution states that “The Council of States shall, as
soon as may be, choose a member of the Council to be Deputy Chairman thereof and,
so often as the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant, the Council shall choose
another member to be Deputy Chairman thereof.”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 89.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 89 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). (राज्यसभा के उपसभापति — अनुच्छेद 89)

 

• Article 89(1) provides that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Article 89(2) contains the exact quoted text — the Rajya Sabha shall choose one of its own members to be the Deputy Chairman, and shall choose another whenever the office falls vacant.

 

• The Deputy Chairman is elected by the members of the Rajya Sabha from amongst themselves and performs the duties of the Chairman when the office of Vice-President is vacant or the Vice-President is acting as President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The corresponding provision for the Lok Sabha's Speaker and Deputy Speaker is Article 93.

 

• Article 90 deals with the vacation, resignation and removal of the Deputy Chairman from office.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 14 (Option 1): Deals with the Right to Equality — equality before law and equal protection of laws.

 

• Article 377 (Option 3): This is a section of the Indian Penal Code (dealing with "unnatural offences"), not an Article of the Constitution relevant here; the Constitution's Article 377 does not correspond to this quoted text.

 

• Article 370 (Option 4): Dealt with the special status of Jammu and Kashmir, abrogated in August 2019.

question: Speed of ______ printer is measured in characters per second (CPS) .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dot Matrix.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Dot Matrix printer is an impact character printer that forms characters using a matrix of pins striking an ink ribbon; its speed is measured in Characters Per Second (CPS). (डॉट मैट्रिक्स प्रिंटर — गति सीपीएस में मापी जाती है)

 

• Dot matrix printers print one character at a time, which is why their speed is naturally expressed per character rather than per page or line.

 

• They are relatively slow and noisy but are still used where multi-part/carbon-copy forms (like invoices and receipts) need to be printed, since the impact mechanism can print through multiple layers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Printer speed units generally correspond to the printer type: CPS for character printers (dot matrix), LPM (Lines Per Minute) for line printers, and PPM (Pages Per Minute) for page printers (laser, inkjet).

 

• Dot matrix printers are a type of impact printer, while laser and inkjet printers are non-impact printers.

 

NOTE

 

• Line (Option 2): A line printer prints an entire line at once; its speed is measured in Lines Per Minute (LPM).

 

• Ink-Jet (Option 3): An inkjet printer is a non-impact printer whose speed is measured in Pages Per Minute (PPM).

 

• Laser (Option 4): A laser printer is also a page printer, with speed measured in Pages Per Minute (PPM).

question: Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile Agni-4 has been successfully test fired in ______.
option_2: Neil Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Agni-4 is a nuclear-capable, Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile (IRBM) developed by DRDO, with a strike range of about 3,000–4,000 km. (अग्नि-4 — मध्यम दूरी की बैलिस्टिक मिसाइल)

 

• It has been repeatedly and successfully test-fired from Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island (formerly known as Wheeler Island), located off the coast of Odisha, as part of routine user trials by the Strategic Forces Command.

 

• The island was renamed in 2015 in honour of former President and renowned scientist Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, who played a key role in India's missile and space programmes.

 

• Agni-series missiles (Agni-I to Agni-V) are surface-to-surface ballistic missiles, forming a key part of India's nuclear deterrent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur, Odisha, on the mainland, is also frequently used along with APJ Abdul Kalam Island for missile testing in the region.

 

• Agni-V, India's longest-range missile in the series (over 5,000 km), has also been tested from the same island.

 

NOTE

 

• Pokhran Firing Range, Rajasthan (Option 1): Known for India's nuclear tests (1974, 1998) and for testing shorter-range missiles/weapon systems, not typically Agni-series IRBM launches.

 

• Neil Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Option 2): A tourist island in the Andaman group, unrelated to missile testing.

 

• Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Home to the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, used for satellite/space launches (ISRO), not for Agni missile test firings.

question: Article 243K of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
option_2: Grounds of disqualification from membership of Panchayat.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Election to the Panchayats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 243K, inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, deals with Elections to the Panchayats. (पंचायतों के लिए निर्वाचन — अनुच्छेद 243K)

 

• It provides for the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the Panchayats to be vested in the State Election Commission.

 

• The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state, and their conditions of service and tenure cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

 

• Part IX of the Constitution (Articles 243–243O), added by the 73rd Amendment, deals comprehensively with the Panchayati Raj system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The corresponding provision for elections to Municipalities is Article 243ZA, found in Part IXA of the Constitution.

 

• The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions, making them mandatory across states (with certain exceptions).

 

NOTE

 

• Durations of panchayat, etc. (Option 1): This is covered under Article 243E, which fixes the term of Panchayats at five years.

 

• Grounds of disqualification from membership of Panchayat (Option 2): This is covered under Article 243F.

 

• Reservation of seats in Panchayat (Option 3): This is covered under Article 243D, which provides for reservation for SCs, STs and women.

question:
In August 2022, Indian Air Force participated in a bilateral exercise named
“Udarashakti” which was hosted by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malaysia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Exercise Udara Shakti 2022 was a bilateral air exercise between the Indian Air Force (IAF) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), conducted in August 2022. (उदय शक्ति — भारत-मलेशिया वायु सेना अभ्यास)

 

• The exercise was hosted by Malaysia, aimed at enhancing interoperability, sharing best practices, and strengthening bilateral defence ties between the two air forces.

 

• IAF fighter aircraft, including Su-30 MKIs, along with support aircraft, participated in the exercise on Malaysian soil.

 

• This exercise reflects India's growing defence cooperation with Southeast Asian nations under its "Act East" policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India conducts several bilateral air exercises with different countries, such as Garuda (with France), Cope India (with the USA), and Indra (with Russia).

 

• "Udara" is a Malay word roughly meaning "air/aerial", reflecting the exercise's focus on air force cooperation.

 

NOTE

 

• UAE (Option 1): India conducts the exercise Desert Eagle with the UAE Air Force, not Udara Shakti.

 

• France (Option 2): India's bilateral air exercise with France is called Exercise Garuda.

 

• USA (Option 4): India's bilateral air exercise with the USA is called Exercise Cope India.

question: Tropical grasslands of Brazil are known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Campos.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The tropical grasslands of Brazil are locally known as Campos. (कैम्पोस — ब्राज़ील के उष्णकटिबंधीय घास के मैदान)

 

• Campos are found mainly on the Brazilian Plateau, and are characterised by tall grasses with scattered trees and shrubs, similar in nature to savanna grasslands elsewhere.

 

• While "Savanna" is the general term used worldwide for tropical grasslands (most famously in Africa), each region often has its own local name.

 

• Other South American grasslands have their own distinct names: the temperate grasslands of Argentina/Uruguay are called Pampas, and the tropical grasslands of the Orinoco basin (Venezuela/Colombia) are called Llanos.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tropical grasslands generally lie between the equatorial rainforests and the hot deserts, in a climate with distinct wet and dry seasons.

 

• Brazil's other major grassland-type ecoregion is the Cerrado, a vast tropical savanna biome known for its rich biodiversity.

 

NOTE

 

• Pampas (Option 1): These are the temperate grasslands of Argentina and Uruguay, not Brazil's tropical grasslands.

 

• Savanna (Option 2): This is the generic global term for tropical grasslands (most associated with Africa), not the specific regional name used in Brazil.

 

• Llanos (Option 3): These are the tropical grasslands found in the Orinoco river basin of Venezuela and Colombia, not Brazil.

question: Who is named as the Missile Man of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam is popularly known as the "Missile Man of India". (मिसाइल मैन ऑफ़ इंडिया — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

 

• He played a pivotal role in the development of India's ballistic missile and space rocket technology, notably as project director of SLV-III (India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle) and as a key figure behind the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP), which produced missiles like Agni and Prithvi.

 

• He served as the 11th President of India (2002–2007) and was widely called the "People's President".

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997, India's highest civilian honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Kalam authored several books, including his autobiography "Wings of Fire".

 

• Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island (formerly Wheeler Island), Odisha, from where several Agni missiles have been test-fired, is named in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram Sarabhai (Option 1): Known as the "Father of the Indian Space Programme"; founder of ISRO.

 

• C. V. Raman (Option 2): An eminent physicist, awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for discovering the "Raman Effect".

 

• Homi Bhabha (Option 4): Known as the "Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme"; founder of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay.

question: 1 terabytes per second = ______ bytes per second
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2^40.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In computer memory/data-storage terminology (binary convention), 1 Tera (T) = 2^40, so 1 terabyte per second = 2^40 bytes per second. (डेटा भंडारण इकाई — 1 टेरा = 2^40)

 

• The binary prefixes used for digital storage, in increasing order, are: Kilo (2^10), Mega (2^20), Giga (2^30), Tera (2^40), Peta (2^50), and so on.

 

• This differs from the decimal (SI) convention sometimes used by hard-drive manufacturers, where 1 Tera = 10^12; but for computer-science/exam purposes, the binary power-of-2 convention (2^40) is used.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1 Kilobyte (KB) = 2^10 bytes = 1024 bytes; 1 Megabyte (MB) = 2^20 bytes; 1 Gigabyte (GB) = 2^30 bytes.

 

• The formal binary units (as per IEC standard) are named Kibi, Mebi, Gibi, Tebi (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB) to distinguish them from the decimal SI units, though "KB, MB, GB, TB" remain in common everyday usage for both.

 

NOTE

 

• 2^10 (Option 2): This is the value of 1 Kilo, not Tera.

 

• 2^20 (Option 3): This is the value of 1 Mega, not Tera.

 

• 2^30 (Option 4): This is the value of 1 Giga, not Tera.

question: Which among the following books is written by Amitav Ghosh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jungle Nama.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Jungle Nama" (2021) is a book by acclaimed Indian author Amitav Ghosh, written in verse, retelling the legend of Bon Bibi, the guardian spirit of the Sundarbans forest. (जंगल नामा — अमिताव घोष)

 

• Amitav Ghosh is a renowned Indian writer known for works such as "The Shadow Lines", "The Glass Palace", "The Hungry Tide", and the Ibis Trilogy (Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, Flood of Fire).

 

• He was the first English-language writer to receive the Jnanpith Award (India's highest literary honour), in 2018.

 

• He has also received the Padma Shri (2007) for his contribution to literature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghosh's non-fiction work "The Great Derangement" (2016) deals with climate change, while "The Nutmeg's Curse" (2021) explores colonialism and the environment.

 

• "Jungle Nama" was illustrated by artist Salman Toor and released as an audiobook narrated by actor Ali Fazal.

 

NOTE

 

• Back to the Roads (Option 1): Not a known work of Amitav Ghosh; not associated with this author.

 

• 400 Days (Option 2): Not a known work of Amitav Ghosh; not associated with this author.

 

• Battlefield (Option 4): Not a known work of Amitav Ghosh; not associated with this author.

question: Who among the following was a ruler of Shunga dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pushyamitra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pushyamitra Shunga was the founder of the Shunga dynasty, which he established around 185 BCE after assassinating the last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha. (पुष्यमित्र शुंग — शुंग वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• The Shunga dynasty ruled parts of north and central India, with its capital initially at Pataliputra, later shifting to Vidisha.

 

• The Shunga period is notable for the construction/expansion of the Sanchi Stupa's gateways (toranas) and railings, and for a revival of Brahmanical traditions after the Mauryan patronage of Buddhism.

 

• Patanjali, the grammarian, is believed to have composed the Mahabhashya during the reign of Pushyamitra Shunga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Shunga dynasty was eventually succeeded by the Kanva dynasty around 73 BCE.

 

• Notable Shunga rulers after Pushyamitra include Agnimitra (his son) and Vasumitra.

 

NOTE

 

• Porus (Option 1): An ancient Indian king who fought Alexander the Great at the Battle of the Hydaspes (326 BCE); unrelated to the Shunga dynasty.

 

• Bindusara (Option 3): The second Mauryan emperor, son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka; a Mauryan, not Shunga, ruler.

 

• Ashoka (Option 4): The most famous Mauryan emperor, known for his edicts and adoption of Buddhism; not a Shunga ruler.

question: Which of the following countries did NOT qualify for the FIFA World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Italy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Italy failed to qualify for the FIFA World Cup 2022 (held in Qatar), losing in the European play-off semi-final to North Macedonia in March 2022 — this was Italy's second consecutive World Cup miss (after also missing 2018). (इटली — फीफा विश्व कप 2022 के लिए क्वालीफाई नहीं कर सका)

 

• This was a major shock, as Italy were the reigning UEFA European champions (Euro 2020, won in 2021) at the time.

 

• Poland, Mexico, and Senegal all successfully qualified and competed in the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar.

 

• Senegal, the reigning Africa Cup of Nations champions, and Poland, led by star striker Robert Lewandowski, both reached the tournament's group stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was won by Argentina, defeating France in the final (on penalties), with Lionel Messi winning the Golden Ball.

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was the first World Cup held in the Middle East and the first held in the winter (November–December).

 

NOTE

 

• Poland (Option 2): Qualified for the 2022 World Cup and reached the Round of 16.

 

• Mexico (Option 3): Qualified for the 2022 World Cup but was eliminated in the group stage.

 

• Senegal (Option 4): Qualified for the 2022 World Cup and reached the Round of 16.

question:
Which among the following companies made an Initial Public Offering (IPO) in Indian
stock market in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adani Wilmar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Adani Wilmar Limited, the FMCG joint venture behind the "Fortune" edible oil brand, launched its Initial Public Offering (IPO) in January 2022, and its shares were listed on the BSE and NSE in February 2022. (आदाणी विल्मर — 2022 का आईपीओ)

 

• The Adani Wilmar IPO was one of the notable IPOs in the Indian stock market during 2022, raising around ₹3,600 crore.

 

• HDFC Bank, JSW Steel, and Avenue Supermarts (DMart) were all already publicly listed companies well before 2022, so none of them launched an IPO that year.

 

• Avenue Supermarts (DMart), promoted by Radhakishan Damani, actually had its IPO back in 2017.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian IPOs around 2021–2022 include Zomato, Paytm (One97 Communications), Nykaa, LIC, and Delhivery.

 

• LIC's IPO (May 2022) was the largest IPO in Indian stock market history at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• HDFC Bank (Option 1): One of India's largest private banks, listed on Indian stock exchanges since 1995.

 

• JSW Steel (Option 2): A major Indian steel company, listed on Indian stock exchanges for decades, not a 2022 IPO.

 

• Avenue Supermarts (Option 3): Parent of the DMart retail chain; its IPO took place in 2017, not 2022.

question:
Before the Partition of Bengal in 1905, Bengal was the biggest province of British
India. It consisted of parts of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and Orissa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Before the Partition of Bengal in 1905, the Bengal Presidency was the largest province of British India, encompassing present-day Bengal, Bihar, Orissa (Odisha), and parts of Assam. (बंगाल विभाजन, 1905 — बिहार और उड़ीसा सहित विशाल प्रांत)

 

• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy, partitioned Bengal (officially for "administrative convenience") into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal (which included Bihar and Orissa), a move widely seen as a "divide and rule" tactic to weaken the nationalist movement.

 

• The partition sparked the Swadeshi Movement and intense public protest, leading to its eventual annulment in 1911, when Bengal was reunited and Bihar and Orissa were carved out as a separate province.

 

• Bihar and Orissa were separated from Bengal as an independent province in 1912, and Orissa was further separated from Bihar in 1936.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1911 Delhi Durbar, where King George V announced the annulment of Bengal's partition, also announced the shifting of India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

 

• The Swadeshi Movement, launched in response to the partition, promoted the boycott of British goods and encouraged indigenous industries.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Orissa (Option 1): Incorrect combination; Uttar Pradesh (then United Provinces) was a separate province, not part of the old Bengal Presidency.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Bihar (Option 2): Incorrect combination; Uttar Pradesh was not part of the Bengal Presidency.

 

• Bihar and Chhattisgarh (Option 4): Incorrect; Chhattisgarh was historically part of the Central Provinces, not the Bengal Presidency.

question: Which of the following sports was NOT played at Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shooting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, and notably excluded Shooting from its sports programme — a decision that drew criticism, especially since India has traditionally won many medals in shooting at the Games. (2022 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — बर्मिंघम, शूटिंग को शामिल नहीं किया गया)

 

• Badminton, Wrestling, and Cricket (T20) were all part of the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

 

• Women's T20 Cricket made its debut at the Commonwealth Games in 2022, with the Australian team winning the gold medal (defeating India in the final).

 

• India finished 4th in the overall medal tally at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, with 61 medals including 22 gold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Due to shooting's exclusion, the Commonwealth Shooting and Archery Championships were held separately in Chandigarh, India, in 2022, with results counted toward that year's overall Commonwealth Games standings for shooting/archery events.

 

• The next Commonwealth Games is scheduled for 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 2): Was contested at the 2022 Commonwealth Games; India won gold in the men's team event and other medals.

 

• Wrestling (Option 3): Was contested at the 2022 Commonwealth Games; India won multiple gold medals in wrestling.

 

• Cricket T20 (Option 4): Made its Commonwealth Games debut (women's event) in 2022.

question:
______ species are the species which are not found after searches of known or likely
areas where they may occur.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Extinct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the IUCN Red List classification, a species is categorised as "Extinct (EX)" when there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, typically established through exhaustive surveys of known and/or expected habitats, at appropriate times, throughout its historic range. (विलुप्त प्रजाति — IUCN की रेड लिस्ट श्रेणी)

 

• The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species categorises species along a scale, including (from least to most at risk of extinction, among threatened categories): Least Concern, Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, Critically Endangered, Extinct in the Wild, and Extinct.

 

• Examples of extinct species include the Dodo, the Passenger Pigeon, and the Tasmanian Tiger (Thylacine).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related category, "Extinct in the Wild (EW)", applies when a species survives only in captivity or as a naturalised population well outside its past range.

 

• The IUCN Red List is maintained by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, headquartered in Gland, Switzerland.

 

NOTE

 

• Endangered (Option 2): A species facing a very high risk of extinction in the wild in the near future, but not yet confirmed extinct.

 

• Normal (Option 3): Not a recognised IUCN Red List conservation category.

 

• Vulnerable (Option 4): A species facing a high risk of extinction in the wild in the medium-term future — a lower risk level than Endangered or Critically Endangered.

question: Which of these books is written by Shashi Tharoor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Why I am Hindu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Why I Am a Hindu" (2018) is a book by Dr. Shashi Tharoor, in which he explores and explains his personal understanding of Hindu philosophy and religion, while also critiquing "political Hindutva". (शशि थरूर — भारतीय राजनयिक, लेखक और सांसद)

 

• Shashi Tharoor is an Indian politician (Member of Parliament from Thiruvananthapuram), former Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations, and a prolific author.

 

• His other notable books include "An Era of Darkness", "Inglorious Empire", "The Great Indian Novel", and "Pax Indica".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tharoor is well known for his extensive English vocabulary and for popularising the word "farrago" through a viral tweet.

 

• He has received several literary honours, including being a finalist for the Commonwealth Writers' Prize.

 

NOTE

 

• A State of Freedom (Option 1): Written by Indian author Neel Mukherjee, not Shashi Tharoor.

 

• Autumn (Option 3): "Autumn" is a novel by British author Ali Smith, not associated with Shashi Tharoor.

 

• Songs of a Coward (Option 4): Written by Indian poet Ranjit Hoskote, not Shashi Tharoor.

question: Which among the following is NOT a component of Lion Capital at Sarnath, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carved cow representing South direction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lion Capital of Ashoka, originally erected atop an Ashokan pillar at Sarnath, consists of four lions standing back to back on an abacus (drum-shaped base), which in turn rests on an inverted lotus (bell-shaped) base. (सारनाथ का सिंह शीर्ष — भारत का राष्ट्रीय प्रतीक)

 

• The abacus is carved with four animals — an elephant, a horse, a bull (zebu), and a lion — each separated by small Dharma Chakras (wheels); a cow is NOT among these four carved animals.

 

• The Lion Capital was adopted as the National Emblem of India on 26 January 1950, showing only three of the four lions (the fourth is hidden from view), along with the Dharma Chakra and the motto "Satyameva Jayate".

 

• It was originally erected by Emperor Ashoka around 250 BCE to commemorate the site of Buddha's first sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath, and today it is preserved at the Sarnath Museum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sarnath Museum, where the original Lion Capital is kept, is the oldest site museum of the Archaeological Survey of India.

 

• The words "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth alone triumphs) beneath the emblem are taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

 

NOTE

 

• Figures of 4 lions (Option 2): A genuine component — four lions stand back-to-back atop the capital.

 

• Dharma Chakras (Option 3): Genuine components — wheels separating the four animal figures on the abacus.

 

• Lotus base bell (Option 4): A genuine component — the inverted bell-shaped lotus forms the base of the capital.

question: Which part of human brain is responsible for walking in straight line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cerebellum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cerebellum ("little brain"), located at the back of the brain beneath the cerebrum, is primarily responsible for coordination of voluntary movements, balance, posture, and motor learning — including the ability to walk in a straight line. (अनुमस्तिष्क — संतुलन और समन्वय के लिए जिम्मेदार)

 

• Damage or impairment of the cerebellum (e.g., due to alcohol intoxication or cerebellar disorders) causes a loss of coordination and balance, resulting in an unsteady, staggering gait — which is why field sobriety tests often assess this cerebellar function.

 

• The cerebellum works by continuously receiving sensory feedback from muscles and joints and comparing it with signals from the motor cortex to fine-tune movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The human brain is broadly divided into the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem (which includes the medulla oblongata, pons, and midbrain).

 

• The cerebellum accounts for roughly 10% of the brain's total volume but contains more than half of the brain's total neurons.

 

NOTE

 

• Medulla (Option 1): The medulla oblongata, part of the brainstem, controls involuntary/autonomic functions like heart rate, breathing, and blood pressure.

 

• Cerebrum (Option 2): The largest part of the brain, responsible for higher functions like thinking, memory, voluntary movement initiation, and sensory perception — but not specifically balance/coordination.

 

• Pons (Option 3): Part of the brainstem, involved in relaying signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum, and regulating functions like sleep and breathing.

question:
Who among the following has been elected as the new President of the Board of
Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roger Binny.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roger Binny, a member of India's 1983 Cricket World Cup-winning team, was elected as the President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in October 2022, succeeding Sourav Ganguly. (रोजर बिन्नी — बीसीसीआई अध्यक्ष, अक्टूबर 2022)

 

• He was elected unopposed at the BCCI's Annual General Meeting (AGM) held on 18 October 2022.

 

• Roger Binny was the leading wicket-taker for India in the 1983 World Cup, which India won under the captaincy of Kapil Dev.

 

• Along with Binny, Jay Shah continued as BCCI Secretary and Arun Dhumal as Treasurer in the reshuffled BCCI office-bearers' team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roger Binny's son, Stuart Binny, has also played cricket for India.

 

• The BCCI is headquartered in Mumbai and governs cricket in India; it is also one of the wealthiest cricket boards in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Sachin Tendulkar (Option 2): A legendary Indian batsman and former captain; he was not elected BCCI President in October 2022.

 

• Kapil Dev (Option 3): Captain of India's 1983 World Cup-winning team; he was not elected BCCI President in October 2022 (he had earlier served as chief of the Cricket Advisory Committee).

 

• Ravi Shastri (Option 4): Former India head coach and cricketer; he was not elected BCCI President in October 2022.

question:
The Indira Sagar Dam is built over river Narmada in which of the following states of
India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indira Sagar Dam is a large multipurpose masonry gravity dam built on the Narmada River near Punasa village in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh. (इंदिरा सागर बांध — नर्मदा नदी, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• It is one of the largest reservoirs in India by volume and is a key project in the Narmada Valley Development Project, providing irrigation, hydroelectric power, and flood control.

 

• The dam has an installed hydroelectric capacity of about 1,000 MW.

 

• The Narmada River originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sardar Sarovar Dam, another major dam on the Narmada, is located further downstream in Gujarat.

 

• The Narmada is one of the few major Indian rivers that flows from east to west, along a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): The Narmada does not flow through Karnataka; major Karnataka rivers include the Krishna, Kaveri and Tungabhadra.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): While the Narmada does flow through Gujarat (where the Sardar Sarovar Dam is located), the Indira Sagar Dam specifically is in Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): The Narmada does not flow through Kerala; major Kerala rivers include the Periyar and Bharathapuzha.

question: Which among the following is a surface-to-surface missile of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agni V.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Agni V is an indigenously developed, nuclear-capable surface-to-surface intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), developed by DRDO, with a strike range of over 5,000 km. (अग्नि-V — भारत की स्वदेशी अंतरमहाद्वीपीय बैलिस्टिक मिसाइल)

 

• It is the longest-range missile in India's Agni series and can be launched from a road-mobile launcher, giving it flexibility and reducing vulnerability.

 

• Agni V uses a three-stage, solid-fuelled propulsion system and employs MIRV (Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicle) technology in its more advanced tests.

 

• Being a surface-to-surface missile, it is launched from and strikes ground-based targets, unlike air-to-air or anti-tank missiles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Agni V has been successfully test-fired multiple times, including from Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha.

 

• India's Agni missile series (Agni-I to Agni-V, and the developmental Agni-P) collectively forms the backbone of the country's land-based nuclear deterrent.

 

NOTE

 

• Javelin (Option 1): A US-made man-portable anti-tank guided missile, not an Indian missile and not a surface-to-surface strategic missile.

 

• AIM-120 AMRAAM (Option 2): A US-made air-to-air missile, not an Indian missile and not a surface-to-surface missile.

 

• Spike (Option 3): An Israeli-made anti-tank guided missile (used by India under license/import), not a surface-to-surface strategic missile of Indian origin.
